title: migrations schema evolution seeds and deployment
concepts: Migrations record the difference between an EF model and a relational schema. Scaffolding creates proposed operations and a model snapshot; developers must inspect data impact and provider-specific SQL.
Migration files form ordered history. Up applies changes and Down attempts reversal, but destructive or lossy transformations may not be safely reversible.

EF Core 9+ migration locking coordinates EF migration execution, but applying schema changes at application startup still couples availability to DDL, requires elevated credentials, and can cause long startup delays/locks. Production deployment often uses reviewed SQL scripts or migration bundles with a controlled identity.
Idempotent scripts support databases at different migration states, but do not make every operation harmless or guarantee cross-version app compatibility.
Model-managed seed data is part of the model snapshot; runtime seeding is designed for database initialization logic. Data backfills and expand-contract sequences need explicit operational plans.

versionNotes.edition: EF Core 11.0.0 released 2026-11-10; migrations and seeding checked 2026-11-16
items: EF Core 9 introduced migration locking and UseSeeding/UseAsyncSeeding. EF Core CLI tools and migration bundles invoke the synchronous UseSeeding delegate, so configure both sync and async forms. EF Core 11.0.0 shipped 2026-11-10 and adds `dotnet ef database update --add` to scaffold and apply a migration in one step. The EF Core 11 What's New page may retain a stale development banner; use final release notes for release status.
